script: Why is UEFA investigating FC Barcelona? For almost two decades, FC Barcelona was paying money to a man named José María Enríquez Negreira. Normally, this wouldn't be an issue. Clubs have a lot of people that they need to pay money to. But in this case, it was a little suspicious. You see, Negreira was the vice president of Spain's referee committee, so he oversaw officials calling their games. Between 2001 and 2018, Barcelona paid companies linked to Negreira around 8.4 million euros, which immediately sets off a red flag for anyone who sees that. Although the club has always said he was a consultant giving them reports on referees, but despite this explanation, not everyone was convinced that FC Barcelona were telling the truth. Prosecutors believe Barcelona was paying Negreira to influence match results in their favor, yet the prosecutors have a big problem because in Spain, the statute of limitations already expired, meaning Barcelona can't face any domestic sporting consequences. But that doesn't mean Barcelona are off the hook just yet because UEFA operates under its own rules, and their president made it very clear that under UEFA's regulations, nothing has expired and that they started looking into the situation a while back. But then today, this thing reached a whole new level. Real Madrid officially submitted a massive report to UEFA, reportedly around 50,000 pages of evidence, calling for Barcelona to be stripped of every title they won during those 17 years and banned from European competition entirely. Barcelona responded with a statement today saying, "No new proceedings have been opened against them," while Negreira himself will likely never stand trial because his dementia has progressed to the point where he's medically unfit. So whether Barcelona are found guilty for this is remained to be seen, but follow to stay updated.
